headline: Decision Council Activity - Source-Based ESL Debate and Voting
outcomes: Students propose solutions, defend them, challenge classmates, and vote on the strongest decision
The activity develops persuasion language, evidence use, and respectful disagreement
Source material becomes active because students must use it to justify their recommendation
Teachers get a structured debate that ends with a clear class decision instead of drifting discussion
howItWorks: LessonCaptain frames a decision problem connected to the topic or source material
Students propose possible solutions or positions from their own devices
The class challenges, compares, and improves the strongest proposals
Students vote on the final decision and explain which evidence or argument changed their mind
teacherUseCases: After a reading or video, ask students to decide what should happen next and defend the choice
Business English lessons where students practise recommendations, trade-offs, and stakeholder language
Critical-thinking lessons where evidence matters more than quick opinions

faq.q: What makes Decision Council different from a debate?
faq.a: A debate often rewards winning a side. Decision Council pushes students toward a final class recommendation, so they must weigh trade-offs, respond to evidence, and sometimes change position.

faq.q: Can one student use Decision Council?
faq.a: Yes. With one student, the teacher can play the challenger role and ask the student to defend or revise a recommendation. Groups add more competing proposals.
It works best with a source, case, video, or article because students can use evidence. It can also run from a topic if the teacher wants a lighter discussion.

faq.q: How does the vote help language learning?
faq.a: The vote creates a reason to listen. Students need to understand arguments before choosing, then explain why one proposal was stronger than another.

faq.q: How do students submit proposals and votes?
faq.a: No. Students join through a browser link and submit ideas or votes without creating accounts.
